_doc: Environmental and ambient lines for Red Reaches. kind: sign (readable prop, interact), placard (landmark text), wind (ambient subtitle or world bark), overheard (barked from nearby when no NPC is in range). station is a hub/landmark id from red_reaches.json. Gating flags as in red_reaches.json NPC barks.

lines.text: Cable hum, a quarter tone flat. Somebody should walk it.
A cairn of survey stones. The newest is three weeks old.
One flat stone left blank, exactly where a hand would reach.
An Old Road marker. The glyphs match a marker you saw continents away.
Tally knots hang from the crank: one for every cup carried away. None are crossed out.
A hand-wide stone by the well. Names are scratched in, small, in different hands.
A Dominion seal stamped on the cistern lid, bright and new.
Cart ruts, deep and fresh. Somebody here says nothing and remembers everything.
Two empty feed bottles on a transport crate. Small hoof prints around it.
The calf blanket is folded on the crate. The hoof prints lead east.
Survey flags in a perfect line. Every third one has a note tucked in the cleft stick.
A low pylon drone. The slate underfoot ticks in time.
Plate beetles rest against warm slate at dusk, leaning on each other like dropped books.
A permit board. Section nine is underlined in red ink, small, in a clerk's hand.
A chalk arch on the yard wall, half rubbed out. Someone drew a second path inside it.
Your footsteps come back half a second late, as if someone is walking behind you, carefully.
A hum behind the stone. Closed is still working.
One drop, then a long still. The water holds the dark like a held breath.
Broken stumps of the bridge that failed. Locals walk around them in silence.
One sentinel stares at the horizon. When it drops its head, the herd is safe.
Skitter mites trace the outline of a fresh crack and gather there, ticking.
Load marks cut into the rail, one for every crossing the Span has been asked to bear.
Fine red grit sifts down from the wedged boulder. Something up there is still settling.
A coil of spare rope hangs by the well, with a tag: 'Mend before you take.'
